key_insight: BioScore evaluates whether pathology image models capture biologically meaningful cell identities—not just whether they perform well on prediction tasks. It uses spatial gene-expression measurements from the same tissue as a reference.
problem_solved: Standard classification and retrieval benchmarks measure model usefulness but reveal little about the underlying biology represented in image embeddings.
method: Extract patch embeddings from a pathology image encoder.
Use a sparse autoencoder to decompose embeddings into sparse features.
Evaluate how well the representations capture cell identities using matched spatial transcriptomics as the biological reference.
impact: BioScore offers practitioners a biology-grounded way to assess pathology foundation models alongside task-based benchmarks. The supplied abstract is truncated, so specific scoring details and experimental results are unavailable.
visual_elements: Side-by-side tissue image and spatial gene-expression map showing matched locations.
Pipeline diagram: image patches → encoder embeddings → sparse autoencoder → biological evaluation.
Cell-type icons linking image representations to transcriptomic cell identities.
Comparison graphic contrasting task-performance evaluation with biology-grounded evaluation.
paper_title: A gene informed benchmark for BioScoring of pathology foundation models
paper_authors: Paul Vilars, Vincent Quoc-Huy Trinh, Maria Vakalopoulou, Dimitris Samaras, Stergios Christodoulidis
